goal: Determinar el perfil de especificidad y de efectos fuera de blanco de dCas9-p300 en celulas humanas, tanto a nivel de union de las guias como de cambios transcriptomicos globales.

questions.question: According to these sources, what is known specifically about dCas9-p300 (nuclease-dead CRISPRa fusion) off-target binding or off-target transcriptional activation in human cells, as distinct from wild-type Cas9 nuclease off-target cutting?
What guide RNA mismatch tolerance or sequence features have been reported in these sources that predispose dCas9-based systems to bind or activate unintended genomic loci?

What genome-wide profiling methods (e.g., ChIP-seq, CUT&RUN, GUIDE-seq, RNA-seq) do these sources describe for assessing dCas9 or CRISPRa binding specificity and global transcriptomic off-target effects?
How does the specificity profile of dCas9 fusion-based CRISPR activators compare to the off-target profile of catalytically active Cas9 nuclease editing, according to these sources?

What gaps or limitations remain in these sources regarding direct experimental evidence of dCas9-p300-specific off-target binding or off-target transcriptomic changes in human cells (as opposed to general CRISPR-Cas9 off-target literature)?
